task: Preserve a provably canonical prior release-unit materialization branch as immutable audit evidence and deterministically supersede it when fresh exact transaction identity/base requires a different materialization, without force-push, deletion or branch ambiguity.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Live bounded rehearsal replay job 112690517069 reached fresh obligation reconciliation successfully, then encountered the old canonical U01 materialization branch release-unit/dev-control-plane-multi-unit-rehearsal-v1-u01 at af0365ec584e3ec8fa9319526af1aa719af912b3. That branch is rooted at the old base 199f21f274524a7b3688f50e09d2d0e3039f86c8, while fresh exact execution now targets main 3992f848e674cf4bb1fe353e2c5cade59c8a52ad. Existing exact-reuse logic correctly rejects the base drift, but there is no canonical supersession path that preserves the old branch and continues on a fresh branch identity.
observableOutcomes: The executor never force-pushes, deletes or rewrites an older canonical materialization branch.
If the canonical base branch is absent, normal exact materialization behavior is unchanged.
If the canonical base branch already exactly matches the fresh transaction, it is reused as today.

If the canonical base branch differs from the fresh transaction, supersession is allowed only after the remote branch is proven to be the exact materialization of the persisted prior manifest/source identity.
A deterministic superseding branch is derived from the fresh binding identity and selected branchRef is persisted in the active execution state before PR creation.
An existing superseding branch is reusable only when its base/tree/commit-message identity exactly matches the fresh materialization.
Foreign, tampered or ambiguous occupation of either canonical or superseding branch remains fail-closed.
unresolvedRisks: Treating any old release-unit branch as canonical could allow branch squatting to trigger supersession.
A branch name based only on releaseUnitId would collide across fresh target-base/binding changes.
Selecting a superseding branch without persisting it would make CI proof and PR lookup use the wrong head branch.
Reconstructing prior canonical identity must use the persisted prior manifest and exact source commit, not only commit-message prefix.
A retry after creating the superseding branch must reuse it idempotently and must not create another generation.

in: Add deterministic superseding branch derivation from fresh release-unit binding identity.
Add exact remote branch inspection/validation reusable for both fresh and prior canonical materializations.
Reconstruct and prove the persisted prior materialization against its old target base and original source commit before allowing supersession.
Create or exact-reuse the deterministic superseding branch without modifying the prior branch.
Persist the selected superseding branchRef into executionTransaction before MATERIALIZED/PR_OPEN.
Add regression tests for canonical prior supersession, exact superseding reuse, branch squatting/tamper rejection and no-force-push behavior.
out: No deletion, rename or force-push of existing release-unit branches.
No manual release-state rewrite or blocker clearing.
No manual child PR creation or receipt fabrication.
No change to child proof, fresh obligation reconciliation, decomposition, Atlas, Release Risk, storefront, database, deployment, auth, payments, inventory, Builder or templates.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This changes branch identity selection inside the trusted write-capable release executor. It must preserve immutable audit evidence while preventing branch squatting or stale remote state from being accepted as a valid successor execution.

acceptanceCriteria: A fresh materialization still uses the canonical base branch when that branch is absent.
An exact existing canonical base branch is reused without push.
A non-exact canonical base branch may trigger supersession only when it exactly matches a reconstructed prior canonical materialization from persisted prior manifest + exact source commit.
Superseding branch name is deterministic from canonical base branch plus fresh binding identity and remains stable across retries.
Fresh receipt is pushed to absent superseding branch without force; exact pre-existing superseding branch is reused; drifted superseding branch blocks.
The selected branchRef is written into executionTransaction and the same branch is used for PR creation and later exact CI proof lookup.
No existing branch is deleted, overwritten or force-pushed.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle close before merge, then unchanged rehearsal resumes from persisted CAS state.
invariants: Prior materialization branch is immutable audit evidence.
Supersession is impossible without proof of prior canonical branch identity.
Branch selection is deterministic from exact fresh transaction identity.
Selected branchRef and materialized head/PR/CI identity refer to the same execution generation.
Remote branch drift is never repaired by force.
CAS state remains the only authoritative persisted execution state.

failureModes: Old canonical branch exists on an obsolete target base.
Old branch looks related by name but is not reconstructably canonical.
Fresh deterministic superseding branch already exists but moved or has wrong tree/message.
Selected branch is not persisted before PR/CI handoff.
Retry creates a second supersession generation despite unchanged fresh binding identity.
edgeCases: Canonical branch exactly equals fresh receipt.
Canonical branch equals reconstructed prior receipt and superseding branch absent.
Canonical branch equals reconstructed prior receipt and superseding branch exactly exists.
Fresh binding digest changes again after later main/policy evolution.

alternatives.summary: Prove the old branch as prior canonical evidence, then choose an immutable fresh branch derived from current binding identity.
alternatives.reason: Preserves audit history and exact transaction identity without weakening remote-branch drift checks.

alternatives.summary: Force-push the original release-unit branch to the fresh materialization.
alternatives.reason: Destroys audit evidence and reintroduces the non-fast-forward/rerun defect the executor was designed to prevent.

alternatives.summary: Delete the old branch and recreate it from fresh base.
alternatives.reason: Makes historical execution evidence mutable and ambiguous.

alternatives.summary: Create a timestamp/random suffix on each retry.
alternatives.reason: Breaks resumability and deterministic PR/CI binding.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing edge is branch-generation identity after a canonical prior materialization becomes stale; the materializer itself remains correct.
specialistReviews.resolution: Insert deterministic branch selection between sealed materialization receipt creation and remote reconciliation, and persist the chosen branchRef.

specialistReviews.finding: Supersession based only on branch name/base mismatch could let a foreign branch cause trusted executor branch creation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require exact reconstruction of prior persisted manifest materialization including old base, tree and canonical commit message before supersession.

specialistReviews.finding: PR and CI proof lookup already key off executionTransaction.branchRef, so that field must hold the selected superseding branch before MATERIALIZED/PR_OPEN.
specialistReviews.resolution: Persist branchRef into the active execution object immediately after exact branch reconciliation and before applying MATERIALIZED event.

specialistReviews.finding: Live rehearsal #1017 proves exact remote reuse is correct but incomplete when a valid previous generation occupies the canonical branch.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add prior-generation canonical proof + deterministic supersession replay tests and rerun the unchanged persisted rehearsal.

challenge.scenario: The canonical release-unit branch exists on an old base and is exactly reproducible from the persisted old manifest/source.
challenge.finding: Current reconcileExactMaterializedCommit correctly throws BASE_DRIFT but provides no immutable continuation path.
challenge.resolution: Select deterministic superseding branch from fresh binding identity only after prior canonical proof passes.

challenge.scenario: A foreign commit occupies the canonical branch but happens to have the expected old parent SHA.
challenge.finding: Base equality alone does not prove canonical prior materialization.
challenge.resolution: Require remote tree and exact canonical releaseUnitCommitMessage to match the reconstructed prior sealed receipt.

challenge.scenario: A retry sees the same fresh transaction after the superseding branch was already pushed.
challenge.finding: Creating a new branch generation would fork execution identity.
challenge.resolution: Derive branch suffix deterministically from fresh binding digest and exact-reuse the branch through existing remote tree/message/base checks.

challenge.scenario: A foreign/tampered commit already occupies the deterministic superseding branch.
challenge.finding: Blind push would either fail ambiguously or overwrite evidence.
challenge.resolution: Use normal non-force push only when absent; if present, exact reconciliation must pass or block.

challenge.scenario: Superseding branch is selected but executionTransaction.branchRef remains the canonical base branch.
challenge.finding: PR creation and proof import would bind to the wrong branch even if head SHA is correct.
challenge.resolution: Persist selected branchRef into execution state before MATERIALIZED and PR_OPEN events.

challenge.scenario: Fresh transaction later changes again and the prior superseding branch remains.
challenge.finding: A fixed '-v2' suffix would collide with the next exact identity.
challenge.resolution: Use fresh binding digest in the branch suffix so each materially distinct exact transaction has one deterministic generation.

challenge.scenario: Base branch is already exact for the fresh transaction.
challenge.finding: Supersession would be unnecessary and fragment identity.
challenge.resolution: Retain current exact remote reuse path and supersede only after fresh-exact mismatch plus prior-canonical proof.

challenge.scenario: A brand-new release unit has no remote canonical materialization branch and no superseding branch on origin.
challenge.finding: If supersession selection probes or manufactures a generation suffix before checking branch absence, first-time materialization would unnecessarily diverge from the canonical release-unit branch and downstream PR/CI lookup would change behavior.
challenge.resolution: Remote inspection must return the canonical base branch unchanged when it is absent; the existing non-force initial push path must execute exactly once and no superseding branch lookup or creation may occur in this case.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only and require Plan Before Code PASS before implementation.
Implement remote branch inspection, prior canonical reconstruction, deterministic superseding branch selection and branchRef persistence.
Add positive/retry/adversarial regression tests, including proof that no force-push/delete command is issued.
Require exact-head Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, full tests, TypeScript, build and Completion Truth PASS.
Commit only canonical lifecycle closure metadata and require final exact-head CI PASS.
Merge, verify fresh main CI, then replay the unchanged rehearsal from persisted CAS state and require canonical U01 PR progression.

requirements.requirement: A fresh exact release-unit transaction must be able to supersede a provably canonical stale materialization branch using a deterministic immutable branch identity while preserving old evidence and all exact PR/CI bindings.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Prior or superseding release-unit materialization branches may not be force-pushed or deleted.
A foreign or drifted branch may not be accepted as canonical prior or current materialization.
